segments.text: Trouble you doing to give me 20 seconds to tell you something very important. A 10-year study of 1,000 men found that push-up capacity is a meaningful predictor of heart disease risk. Here is what the data showed. Men who could do 20 or more push-ups were linked to a 75% lower rate of cardiovascular events.

Being able to do 40 or more push-ups was linked to a 96% lower rate. And push-ups outperformed treadmill tests at predicting heart disease. This makes sense because push-ups don't just measure cardio, they capture muscular strength and power, two of the strongest protective biomarkers known for long-term health. One caveat, the study was conducted on young to middle-aged male firefighters. So, the specific numbers don't directly extend to women, senior adults, or sedentary populations.
But, the underlying message is hard to ignore. The heart wants what it wants, and that's 40 push-ups.
